title: Studio atmosphere and an A&R man who stays in the booth
summary: Mingus complains that his Atlantic A&R man cannot read scores or listen in the room; he brought Teo Macero in at his own cost.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: (Recording interrupted.)
Okay? One thing I never asked you about was recording, and what makes for a decent atmosphere, once you get the technology for a good session? Why some studio sessions are cold and some are not?
(Unintelligible) creates an atmosphere. Like, I remember (inaudible).
Yeah.
We'd have drinks and act like we had all day long to do it.
Yeah.
And we'd do two or three albums in one session. Now, you got this guy, (unintelligible).
Mamariglo.

He's got him, and couldn't read those scores, either, but this guy pretends to be a musician, and he can't read the scores. And he never comes out into the room to hear the sound of the music, musically.
That's interesting. You mean, all he hears is what comes into the booth from the mikes.
That's right.
Now, why is it important for him to go out in the room and hear the --
Because it sounds better.
And he'll also know what sound to get.
That's right.
Yeah.
And get the feeling, the feelings in the room.
Yeah.
He has no -- my last date, there was no feeling.
In other words, even when the leader is somebody as strong as you are, if you can't counter effectively an A&R man who acts like that --
No. I brought Tio Macero in because he knew scores, every score, and he don't have influence on . He couldn't work with him. I told Tio I was paying him myself.
Yeah. Couldn't you complain to Nessely?
Nestvi doesn't have anything to do with the company anymore.
Oh, really? Oh, he's upstairs.
(Unintelligible) play last time.
Yeah.
And I hurt his feelings.

Oh, Mimaroglu, yeah. Gee, that's something I haven't thought of, that a guy who by now has the stature you have, is nonetheless forced, if you want to make the record on that label, to take an A&R man who he'd really rather not have.
That's right. And the rock and roll people take months, sometimes years, to record one record. And they expect us to go and do it in one or two days.
What about -- I always figured from the outside --
The disrespect is insulting as anything.
